conflicts.description: The schematic's 4R and 6R location annotations imply four bulbs but print '(3) NO. 89'. Its 8R annotation specifies three playfield bulbs and one insert-panel bulb, while the operator's location drawing and VPW have four playfield candidates. No complete bank quantity is asserted; 8R remains unplaced. Resolution path: a machine owner photographs and counts the populated sockets and wiring on banks 4R, 6R and 8R, or a curator obtains a later factory schematic revision that reconciles the counts.

drivers.variant_notes: This is PinMAME's source root for the audited Star Wars family. Pinned PinMAME 97aa922bf8e4b6970126192ec1ac1fb0305a4f62 records CPU, DE_DMD32ROM8x DMD, and DE2 sound chips with CRC/SHA1 in tools/star_wars_pinmame.json. All eleven drivers share INITGAMES11(stwr,GEN_DEDMD32, de_128x32DMD, FLIP1516, SNDBRD_DE2S, SNDBRD_DEDMD32, 0). The source manifest establishes emulator routing only; physical ROM/socket compatibility remains unknown pending primary-source hardware evidence. Stern's retained official readme (service.star-wars.official-104-readme) dates V1.04 December 19, 2012 and lists a ten-second Freeze ball save, revised ramp/Force scoring, bonus, combo, audio and audit behavior. These rules changes do not establish EPROM/socket compatibility; the full factual change list is excerpted.

physical.notes: Black Advance: momentary service step button, released public 0, pressed 1. PinMAME complements it to PIA2 CA1; do not invert the public value again. Exact-title harness navigation proves ROM acceptance.

Green Forward/Reverse: maintained push-on/push-off service selector. Up/forward is public 0, down/reverse 1; keep that state between Advance pulses. This is the contact's up/released reference, not a spring-return button. Internal LS02/PIA polarity is already handled by PinMAME.

inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP1516 (FLIP_SWNO(15,16)) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8. FLIP1516 sets no FLIP_SOL, FLIP_EOS, or upper FLIP_SW bit, so this exact initializer cannot route the position to the ROM.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP1516 (FLIP_SWNO(15,16)) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 16 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 16: a host write to 16 is overwritten on the next update. The exact initializer declares only the lower right matrix copy at 16; no upper flipper input is declared. The cabinet leaf contact closes to energize its flipper ground circuit, so the released button is normally open. ROM test names the corresponding matrix contact at public 1; synthetic coil pair follows only while output 23 enables it.

The game's CPU sheet labels the PIA 11B PA7 ground jumper J8, factory installed (DIP 0 = 0). pia2a_r reads core_getDip(0) << 7. Its shared Williams W7 comment and S11 Germany/USA labels do not describe this Data East input: DE_COMPORTS declares no Country DIP. No country meaning is asserted. This is not an operator-DIP bank.

mechanisms.behavior: Outhole switch 10 detects a drained ball; coil 1 returns it to the feed trough. Three physical trough contacts 11/12/13 sense the queue; coil 2 ejects its leading ball toward shooter switch 14. Factory names left/center/right are distinct from VPW's virtual array (11,13,12,10). Initialize three balls; do not model switch 10 as a fourth trough contact. A failed eject must leave the actual occupied contact closed for the ROM's retry/search logic.
mechanisms.label: Outhole and Three-Ball Feed Trough

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball closes shooter-lane 14; coil 3 launches it. Shifter fire button 50 is the player's launch/skill-shot control, not the lane occupancy switch. VPW uses cvpmImpulseP; its speed 65 and 0.5 tuning are table physics, not factory travel time.
mechanisms.label: Automatic Ball Launcher

mechanisms.behavior: Hand-operated front-cabinet assembly 500-5620-00 contains the fire/button harness (50), the Shift Down microswitch (51), and a spring. The factory chart explicitly leaves 52 unfitted despite the ROM's SHIFT UP diagnostic label; do not invent another input. VPW's Plunger/LockBar key asserts both 50 and 51 and clears both on release, while Left/Right Magna-Save latch 51 off/on; neither writes 50. These keyboard conveniences do not change the two fitted physical contacts or prove a motorized lever, spring force or travel specification.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet Shifter and Fire Button

mechanisms.behavior: Ball occupancy holds the scoop contact closed until the corresponding eject coil releases the ball back onto the playfield. Keep occupancy during a failed eject. The two scoops have separate switches and coils; do not route them through the VUK counter.
mechanisms.label: Left Force Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Ball occupancy holds the scoop contact closed until the corresponding eject coil releases the ball back onto the playfield. Keep occupancy during a failed eject. The two scoops have separate switches and coils; do not route them through the VUK counter.
mechanisms.label: Right Sarlacc Scoop

mechanisms.behavior: Death Star trough 34 and Obi-Wan trough 35 route balls beneath the playfield to the left VUK 36. Coil 5 lifts a waiting ball to the wire ramp. VPW AddVUK delays its virtual arrival 200ms, counts queued balls, and holds 36 until its queue empties. That counter is a recreation of the shared return, not extra physical switches or measured transit time. A jam leaves the corresponding real occupancy contact closed.
mechanisms.label: Death Star / Obi-Wan Underchute and Left VUK

mechanisms.behavior: Hits drop individual top/middle/bottom targets and close 30/31/32; they stay down and active until coil 6 resets the bank. Reset opens all three after the targets rise. Preserve partially dropped banks and failed resets; fixed X-Wing targets 25-29 do not share this reset.
mechanisms.label: Three-Bank Drop Target Reset

mechanisms.behavior: Motor/relay 12 raises or lowers the entrance bar carrying hit target 40. End contacts 41 UP and 42 DOWN close just before their respective travel limits and must never be on together. VPW models reciprocal travel with vpmMechReverse, 72 steps and marks 0/71, disabling target 40 collision when lowered. These are software marks, not degrees or factory timing. Start with actual bar state and sensor feedback; do not fabricate a successful limit on a jam.
mechanisms.label: Death Star Entrance Bar

mechanisms.behavior: Shared relay 15 drives two separate 28VAC motors: Death Star 515-5570-00 and R2D2 515-5571-00 (R2D2 unit 500-5484-00). No rotation index contact is listed. VPW uses a 360-step circular Death Star model and invokes UpdateR2Head, oscillating artwork between -80 and +60 degrees. These are visual phase/travel choices, not measured factory steps or travel. Turning off the relay stops drive, with table-owned coast tuning. One controller actuator is intentionally owned by this combined drive mechanism.
mechanisms.label: Death Star and R2D2 Rotation Drive

mechanisms.behavior: Coil 9 lifts the R2D2 body; releasing it returns the toy. Switch 38 is the entrance ball switch, not a toy-position sensor. VPW SolR2/UpdateR2 animates height separately from output 15's head rotation. Its height/speed constants are artwork tuning; there is no encoded physical position telemetry.
mechanisms.label: R2D2 Raise / Dance

mechanisms.behavior: When the ROM enables Laser Kick, a ball at left outlane 24 is returned by coil 16; otherwise it drains. VPW pulls back the kickback at initialization, fires on the output's rising state, and retracts on release. Lamp 56 is the lit feature indication, not an actuator.
mechanisms.label: Left Outlane Laser Kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Ball contact closes the scoring/trigger switch and the corresponding special coil kicks the ball away. The physical trigger circuit and ROM diagnostic share this coil; do not assume a host switch closure makes PinMAME synthesize a special output (ssSw is empty). Return the skirt/contact when the ball leaves.
mechanisms.label: Top Turbo Bumper

mechanisms.behavior: Rubber deflection closes the sling switch and the physical special-solenoid circuit kicks the ball. ROM diagnostics publish the named output; ssSw is empty, so a recreation must not rely on PinMAME deriving a kick from a host switch pulse alone.
mechanisms.label: Left Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Rubber deflection closes the sling switch and the physical special-solenoid circuit kicks the ball. ROM diagnostics publish the named output; ssSw is empty, so a recreation must not rely on PinMAME deriving a kick from a host switch pulse alone.
mechanisms.label: Right Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet button drives the solid-state flipper hardware while game-on output 23 enables it. PinMAME supplies identical synthetic power/hold states for this non-CPU-controlled initializer; they do not measure winding duty or EOS. Drive host button 84 left / 82 right and release to return the bat. Physical coil 090-5032-00 (22-1080); table physics determines stroke/return.
mechanisms.label: Left Flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet button drives the solid-state flipper hardware while game-on output 23 enables it. PinMAME supplies identical synthetic power/hold states for this non-CPU-controlled initializer; they do not measure winding duty or EOS. Drive host button 84 left / 82 right and release to return the bat. Physical coil 090-5032-00 (22-1080); table physics determines stroke/return.
mechanisms.label: Right Flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Momentary coil 8 strikes the cabinet knocker. It has no scoring/position switch; release returns the striker. The retained table defines a sound routine without assigning SolCallback(8), an omitted recreation callback rather than evidence of absent factory hardware.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet Knocker
